correctness.rationale: Fink's positive convolution expansion restricts exactly to the divisor-closed monoid generated by a finite prime set \(Q\): if a product lies in that monoid, every factor does too. Hence, whenever \(Z_Q(s)<2\), Tonelli positivity gives \(A_Q(s)=Z_Q(s)/(2-Z_Q(s))\). If \(Z_Q(1)>2\), continuity yields a unique \(\alpha_Q>1\) with \(Z_Q(\alpha_Q)=2\). Assuming every supported integer is non-ample gives \(A_Q(s)\le Z_Q(s-1)\) for \(s>1\); as \(s\downarrow\alpha_Q\), the exact left side diverges while the finite-prime right side stays finite, a contradiction. Fink's supermultiplicative inequality makes all powers of one witness ample, and divergence of the Euler product over primes beyond any fixed cutoff supplies an admissible finite support there. A fresh independent check reproduced the example support product \(1001/384>2\) and \(\alpha_Q\approx1.1843600447\).
residual_risks: The theorem is existential and gives no practical least-witness bound.
The Euler-product criterion is sufficient, not claimed necessary.

originality.rationale: Fink's 2020 primary paper explicitly states as Conjecture 1 that ample numbers should avoid the first \(k\) primes for every \(k\), and proves that one witness gives infinitely many by product closure. His 2023 paper gives the global Dirichlet series and the positive convolution expansion. Neither inspected source restricts that expansion to an arbitrary finite prime-support monoid or uses the resulting finite-support pole to force an ample coefficient. A current problem database still listed the conjecture as open with zero recorded solutions, and current Resultary search returned only the assigned all-\(k\) theorem plus a separate \(k=3\) partial result. The support-local Dirichlet-series argument is therefore a genuine new mechanism rather than a specialization of the global formula.
residual_risks: Literature indexing can lag a very recent independent solution.
The theorem does not identify minimal supports or least witnesses.
